claim: An Amazon EMR cluster is a collection of Amazon EC2 instances, and each instance in the cluster is called a node.
question: What is an Amazon EMR cluster made of?

values.display: a collection of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances
Each instance in the cluster is called a node

evidence.quote: A cluster is a collection of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances. Each instance in the cluster is called a node.

claim: The primary node manages the cluster by coordinating the distribution of data and tasks among other nodes. Every cluster has a primary node, and a single-node cluster with only the primary node is possible.
question: What does the EMR primary node do, and does every cluster have one?

values.display: manages the cluster
Every cluster has a primary node

evidence.quote: A node that manages the cluster by running software components to coordinate the distribution of data and tasks among other nodes for processing.
The primary node tracks the status of tasks and monitors the health of the cluster. Every cluster has a primary node, and it's possible to create a single-node cluster with only the primary node.

claim: A core node runs tasks and stores data in HDFS on the cluster. Multi-node clusters have at least one core node.
question: What do EMR core nodes do?

values.display: run tasks and store data in the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS)
at least one core node

evidence.quote: A node with software components that run tasks and store data in the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) on your cluster. Multi-node clusters have at least one core node.

claim: A task node only runs tasks and does not store data in HDFS. Task nodes are optional.
question: What do EMR task nodes do, and are they required?

values.display: only runs tasks and does not store data in HDFS
Task nodes are optional

evidence.quote: A node with software components that only runs tasks and does not store data in HDFS. Task nodes are optional.

claim: Removing HDFS daemons from a running core node or terminating core nodes risks data loss.
question: Why is it risky to terminate EMR core nodes?

values.display: risks data loss
terminating core nodes

evidence.quote: Removing HDFS daemons from a running core node or terminating core nodes risks data loss.

claim: A cluster has only one core instance group or instance fleet, but it can run multiple nodes on multiple EC2 instances in it.
question: How many core instance groups or fleets does an EMR cluster have?

values.display: only one core instance group or instance fleet per cluster
multiple nodes running on multiple Amazon EC2 instances

evidence.quote: There is only one core instance group or instance fleet per cluster, but there can be multiple nodes running on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in the instance group or instance fleet.

claim: By default, EMR schedules YARN so that application master processes run only on core nodes, so running jobs do not fail when Spot task nodes are terminated.
question: Why do jobs not fail when EMR Spot task nodes are terminated?

values.display: allowing application master processes to run only on core nodes
running jobs do not fail

qualifiers.scope: EMR on EC2 with YARN node labels (default through 5.x releases)

evidence.quote: Because Spot Instances are often used to run task nodes, Amazon EMR has default functionality for scheduling YARN jobs so that running jobs do not fail when task nodes running on Spot Instances are terminated. Amazon EMR does this by allowing application master processes to run only on core nodes.

claim: Beginning with the Amazon EMR 6.x release series, the YARN node labels feature is disabled by default, so application primary processes can run on both core and task nodes unless you enable it.
question: In EMR 6.x, can application masters run on task nodes by default?

values.display: disabled by default
run on both core and task nodes by default

evidence.quote: Beginning with Amazon EMR 6.x release series, the YARN node labels feature is disabled by default. The application primary processes can run on both core and task nodes by default.

claim: With instance fleets, each node type has a single fleet that can contain a mix of instance types, with target capacities for On-Demand and Spot Instances.
question: What is the difference between EMR instance fleets and instance groups?

values.display: a mix of instance types
target capacities for On-Demand and Spot Instances

evidence.quote: With instance groups, each group contains Amazon EC2 instances of the same type, and you can have multiple groups per node type (except primary). With instance fleets, each node type has a single fleet that can contain a mix of instance types, with target capacities for On-Demand and Spot Instances.

claim: For the primary node type in an instance fleet, Amazon EMR chooses a single instance type from your list, and you choose whether it is provisioned as On-Demand or Spot.
question: How does EMR provision the primary node in an instance fleet?

values.display: chooses a single instance type from your list of instances
On-Demand or Spot Instance

evidence.quote: For the primary node type, Amazon EMR chooses a single instance type from your list of instances, and you specify whether it's provisioned as an On-Demand or Spot Instance.

claim: Instance fleets let you set a Spot capacity-optimized allocation strategy and an On-Demand lowest-price allocation strategy, plus a Spot timeout action if capacity cannot be provisioned.
question: Which allocation strategies do EMR instance fleets offer?

values.display: a preferred allocation strategy (capacity-optimized)
allocation strategy (lowest-price)

evidence.quote: Instance fleets also provide additional options for Spot Instance and On-Demand purchases. Spot Instance options include a timeout that specifies an action to take if Spot capacity can't be provisioned, and a preferred allocation strategy (capacity-optimized) for launching Spot Instance fleets. On-Demand Instance fleets can also be launched using the allocation strategy (lowest-price) option.

claim: Uniform instance groups offer a simpler setup than instance fleets, while the instance fleets configuration offers the widest variety of provisioning options.
question: Which EMR configuration is simpler, instance groups or instance fleets?

values.display: simpler setup than instance fleets
widest variety of provisioning options

evidence.quote: The instance fleets configuration offers the widest variety of provisioning options for Amazon EC2 instances.
Uniform instance groups offer a simpler setup than instance fleets.

claim: With uniform instance groups you can only set the purchasing option when you create the group; with instance fleets you can change purchasing options after creating the fleet and mix them to reach a target capacity.
question: Can you change the EMR purchasing option of a running cluster?

values.display: only specify the purchasing option for an instance group when you create it
change purchasing options after you create the instance fleet

qualifiers.scope: EMR on EC2, uniform instance groups versus instance fleets

evidence.quote: If you choose uniform instance groups, you can only specify the purchasing option for an instance group when you create it, and the instance type and purchasing option apply to all Amazon EC2 instances in each instance group. If you choose instance fleets, you can change purchasing options after you create the instance fleet, and you can mix purchasing options to fulfill a target capacity that you specify.

claim: You cannot change an instance purchasing option while a cluster is running: for primary and core nodes you must terminate the cluster and launch a new one, and for task nodes you launch a new task group or fleet and remove the old one.
question: How do you switch EMR nodes between On-Demand and Spot?

values.display: can't change an instance purchasing option while a cluster is running
terminate the cluster and launch a new one

evidence.quote: You can't change an instance purchasing option while a cluster is running. To change from On-Demand to Spot Instances or vice versa, for the primary and core nodes, you must terminate the cluster and launch a new one. For task nodes, you can launch a new task instance group or instance fleet, and remove the old one.

claim: When the primary node terminates the cluster ends, so run the primary node on Spot only when sudden termination is acceptable.
question: When is it acceptable to run the EMR primary node on Spot?

values.display: When it terminates, the cluster ends
sudden termination is acceptable

evidence.quote: The primary node controls and directs the cluster. When it terminates, the cluster ends, so you should only launch the primary node as a Spot Instance if you are running a cluster where sudden termination is acceptable.

claim: Terminating a core instance risks data loss, so run core nodes on Spot only when partial HDFS data loss is tolerable.
question: When is it acceptable to run EMR core nodes on Spot?

values.display: Terminating a core instance risks data loss
partial HDFS data loss is tolerable

evidence.quote: Core nodes process data and store information using HDFS. Terminating a core instance risks data loss. For this reason, you should only run core nodes on Spot Instances when partial HDFS data loss is tolerable.

claim: Task nodes hold no persistent data in HDFS, so if a Spot task node is terminated because the Spot price rose above your maximum, no data is lost and the effect on the cluster is minimal.
question: What happens when an EMR Spot task node is terminated?

values.display: do not hold persistent data in HDFS
no data is lost

evidence.quote: The task nodes process data but do not hold persistent data in HDFS. If they terminate because the Spot price has risen above your maximum Spot price, no data is lost and the effect on your cluster is minimal.

claim: When a core instance group uses Spot Instances, EMR waits until it can provision all requested core instances before launching the group, whereas a task instance group launches with as many Spot nodes as it can get.
question: Does an EMR core group launch if only some Spot instances are available?

values.display: waits until it can provision all of the requested core instances
provisions as many task nodes as it can

evidence.quote: When you launch the core instance group as Spot Instances, Amazon EMR waits until it can provision all of the requested core instances before launching the instance group.
When you launch one or more task instance groups as Spot Instances, Amazon EMR provisions as many task nodes as it can, using your maximum Spot price.

claim: You can only add a Spot Instance primary node when you launch the cluster, and you cannot add or remove primary nodes from a running cluster.
question: Can you add a primary node to a running EMR cluster?

values.display: only add a Spot Instance primary node when you launch the cluster
can't add or remove primary nodes from a running cluster

evidence.quote: You can only add a Spot Instance primary node when you launch the cluster. You can't add or remove primary nodes from a running cluster.

claim: You can run multiple instance groups, using On-Demand Instances in one group for guaranteed processing power and Spot Instances in another to finish jobs faster and at lower cost.
question: How do you combine On-Demand and Spot in one EMR cluster?

values.display: On-Demand Instances in one group for guaranteed processing power
Spot Instances in another group

evidence.quote: Amazon EMR also provides the option to run multiple instance groups so that you can use On-Demand Instances in one group for guaranteed processing power together with Spot Instances in another group to have your jobs completed faster and at lower costs.

claim: An EMR cluster in a private subnet without VPC endpoints for Amazon S3 incurs additional NAT gateway charges for S3 traffic, because that traffic does not stay within the VPC.
question: How do you avoid NAT gateway charges for EMR traffic to S3?

values.display: VPC endpoints for Amazon S3
additional NAT gateway charges

evidence.quote: If your EMR cluster is in a private subnet without VPC endpoints for Amazon S3, you will incur additional NAT gateway charges that are associated with S3 traffic because the traffic between your EMR cluster and S3 will not stay within your VPC.
